quiz: Aggregates like AVG skip NULL values entirely. Average only the values that are actually present.
Without GROUP BY an aggregate query always returns one row. Think about what SUM gives over an empty set, unlike COUNT.
COUNT(DISTINCT) ignores NULLs and counts each repeated value only once.
Look for a selected column that is neither grouped nor aggregated. Strict engines reject it; a loose one picks any value.
Recall which clause runs per row before any grouping has happened, so aggregates do not exist yet.
GROUP BY treats NULLs as equal to each other, the same way DISTINCT does.
CASE checks branches top to bottom and stops at the first TRUE one.
The simple CASE form compares with =, and anything = NULL is UNKNOWN, never TRUE.
COUNT counts every non-NULL value, and 0 is not NULL.
NULLIF(a, b) gives NULL when the two arguments are equal, otherwise a.
COALESCE scans its arguments left to right and returns the first one that is not NULL.
After COALESCE turns NULLs into 0, every employee is in the average, so divide the total by all rows.
When both sides are integers, SQLite does integer division and drops the fraction.
Think of the steps: produce rows, filter rows, group, filter groups, pick columns, then sort.
